title: Closed points of decent spaces are closed field subspaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with field-valued point classes and atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology] and sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A field is as in [def-weil-field] and its spectrum as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. A field-valued morphism $u:\operatorname{Spec}F\to X$ is quasi-compact if for every affine scheme $U\to X$ the scheme $U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}F$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Assume every field-valued morphism to $X$ is quasi-compact, and let $x\in|X|$ be a closed point, meaning that $\{x\}$ is closed. There exist a field $K$ and an $S$-morphism $i:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ with image $\{x\}$ such that $i$ is a representable closed immersion: for every scheme $T\to X$, the fibre product $T\times_X\operatorname{Spec}K$ is a scheme and its projection to $T$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Tag 0AHB (lemma-decent-space-closed-point); decency is Tag 03I8 (definition-very-reasonable), equivalently Tag 03JV (lemma-UR-finite-above-x), condition (6).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-decent-quasicompact-monomorphic-points] to choose a quasi-compact monomorphism $i:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ representing $x$. Apply the same assertion at every point of $X$; its conclusion supplies the hypothesis of [lem-sfb-decent-etale-fibres-no-specializations]. Let $p:U\to X$ be an affine etale chart. Such charts jointly cover $X$: an atlas exists by [def-trf-algebraic-space], and its scheme source has an affine open cover by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis].

source.place: Tag 0AHB, first two sentences; Tag 03JV (6) implies (4).

proof.text: The set $F=p^{-1}(\{x\})$ is closed by the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. For $u\in F$, every specialization $u\leadsto v$ lies in $F$; [lem-sfb-decent-etale-fibres-no-specializations] gives $v=u$. Thus $\overline{\{u\}}=\{u\}$: each point of $F$ is closed in $U$. Form $W=U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}K$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] it is a scheme etale over $K$. It is quasi-compact by our choice of $i$ and affineness of $U$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] to $W\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ identifies $W$ with a disjoint union of spectra of fields; its singleton opens cover it, so quasi-compactness makes the union finite. Write $W=\coprod_{a=1}^r\operatorname{Spec}L_a$.

source.place: Tag 0AHB, closedness of chart fibre points and finite field decomposition; Tag 02GL.

proof.text: The projection $q:W\to U$ is monomorphic: equal $U$ components give equal composites to $X$, hence equal $\operatorname{Spec}K$ components by monomorphy of $i$, and equal maps to the pullback. Fix a component image $u\in F$. It is closed by step 2, so its canonical map $j_u:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$ is a closed immersion by [lem-trf-closed-point-residue-immersion]. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field], every component mapping to $u$ factors through $j_u$; uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-field-point-factors-through-immersion] shows its pullback along $j_u$ is that same component. Components mapping elsewhere have empty pullback, since $j_u$ has image $\{u\}$. Thus $W_u$ is exactly the coproduct of the components mapping to $u$. Its map to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ is monomorphic by the pullback argument above. Apply [lem-sfb-monomorphism-into-field-coproduct] with the one field $\kappa(u)$: the nonempty $W_u$ is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ over that spectrum. Consequently exactly one component maps to $u$ and its map $\kappa(u)\to L_a$ is an isomorphism. Therefore the component maps are closed immersions with pairwise distinct images.

source.place: Tag 0AHB, monomorphism, distinct component images and residue fields; schemes.tex Tags 03DP and 01J9.

proof.text: The finitely many images $u_a$ are pairwise distinct closed points. Their union is closed, and its induced topology is discrete since the complement of the other finitely many points isolates each $u_a$. Hence $q$ is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset. Its structure-sheaf map is surjective locally: away from the finite union its target sheaf is zero; near $u_a$ remove all other $u_b$, so the map is exactly the restriction of the closed immersion from the $a$th component proved in step 3. Surjectivity of a sheaf map is local by its definition (sections lift on a covering). Therefore $q$ is a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This includes $r=0$, when the source is empty.

source.place: Tag 0AHB, sentence about pairwise distinct closed points; closed-immersion definition.

proof.text: Step 4 applies to each affine chart in the jointly surjective etale family of step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-atlas-locality] to $i$ and that family. It gives that $i$ is representable and every scheme base change is a closed immersion. The chosen representative has image $\{x\}$, as required.

source.place: Tag 0AHB, final descent; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03M4 (4) implies (1).

Step 2: the chart fibre is closed by the final topology, its points are closed by the new node, W is a scheme etale and quasi-compact over K, and 02GL gives finitely many field spectra. Step 3: q is a monomorphism, 01J9 factors each component through the closed immersion j_u, and 03DP with one field shows exactly one component lies over each point with kappa(u) isomorphic to L_a. The use of j_u being a monomorphism for non-field tests is elementary (a closed immersion is a monomorphism). Step 4 is correctly marked elementary: a finite disjoint union of closed immersions with distinct closed images, including r=0. Step 5 applies 03M4 locality to the jointly surjective affine family, with no representability assumed in advance. Batch 5: the atlas-locality node, def-trf-algebraic-space and def-a1-space-point-topology reach sec-trace-formula only through the general definition of algebraic spaces and their point topology. lean.statement: theorem exists_closedImmersion_field_of_decent {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (hdecent : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] (b : Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ S) (c : yoneda.obj (Over.mk b) ⟶ X.obj.obj) (U : Over S), IsAffine U.left → ∀ t : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj, ∃ (V : Over S) (p : V ⟶ U) (q : yoneda.obj V ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk b)), IsPullback q (yoneda.map p) c t ∧ CompactSpace V.left) (x : Point X.obj.obj) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set (Point X.obj.obj))) : ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (b : Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ S) (i : yoneda.obj (Over.mk b) ⟶ X.obj.obj), pointImage i = {x} ∧ IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) i
